summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Sayadaw U Sīlānanda studied at University College, Colombo, and under U Paññāvanta and Mahasi Sayadaw. He taught at the University of Mandalay (~1960–1969), founded Dhammānanda Vihara, and served as Chancellor of the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University (1999).

Sayadaw U Thittila was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ashin Adiccavamsa and at Visva-Bharati University (~1934–1937). He served as a librarian at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1937–1938) and taught Buddhist philosophy at the University of Rangoon (1952).

Working in Buddhist and religious studies, Sayagyi U Ba Khin studied under Saya Thetgyi (Sayagyi Thet Gyi) from ~1937 to 1945. He founded the International Meditation Centre and taught prominent students including Satya Narayan Goenka and Mother Sayamagyi.
Sayaka Sonoda completed PhD studies at Toyo University (attested 2015–2016) under the supervision of Shinobu Yamaguchi and co-supervisor Shogo Watanabe.
Specializing in Indology, Sayori Tsubota was a PhD student at Osaka University (attested 2020) and later served as a JSPS Postdoctoral Fellow (PD) at Tohoku University (attested 2026).

Working in Buddhist and religious studies, Scott A. Mitchell earned his PhD at the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne (attested 2008). He became a professor and president at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and joined the Numata Center.

Specializing in linguistics and Tibetology, Scott DeLancey studied under Yungdrung Manang. He held academic posts at the University of Colorado Boulder (~1980–1982) and the University of Oregon (~1982).
Specializing in Buddhist studies and Sinology, Scott Hurley earned his PhD from the University of Arizona in 2001, where he studied under Elizabeth Harrison.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, Scott Pacey earned his doctorate from the Australian National University (2011). He held posts at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, the Australian National University, and the University of Manchester (attested 2014).

Sean D. Gaffney specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at SOAS University of London under Philip Denwood, Renate Söhnen-Thieme, Alexander Piatigorsky, David Seyfort Ruegg, and doctoral supervisor Tadeusz Skorupski, later holding a post at SOAS (attested 1996).

Working in Buddhist studies and Indology, Sebastian Nehrdich earned his MA at the University of Hamburg (attested 2019) and also studied at Kyoto University. He has held positions at Tohoku University and as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg.
Sebastian Pole works in Indology and related fields. He completed his studies at the East West College of Herbalism, the London College of Oriental Medicine, and the College of Ayurveda.
Specializing in Buddhist studies, See Mui Yian pursued a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).

Historian Seema Alavi earned her doctorate at the University of Cambridge (~1986–1991). She held teaching and professorial appointments at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1992–1994), Jamia Millia Islamia (~1994–2007), the University of Delhi (~2007–2021), and Ashoka University (~2021).

Working in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, Seigai Omura studied at Tokyo University of the Arts under Kanō Tomonobu and Umpei Shinma. He served as professor at Tokyo University of the Arts (1905) and founded the Bussho Kankōkai.

Specializing in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, Seiichi Mizuno earned his doctorate and studied under Kosaku Hamada at Kyoto University. He held posts at Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities and was a university professor (1949–1968).

A scholar in religious studies and philosophy, Seiichi Yagi studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1955). He held faculty posts at Kanto Gakuin University (~1956–1968), Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1968–1993), and Toin University of Yokohama (~1993–2002).

Seiichiro Ono studied at the University of Tokyo under Eiichi Makino, earning a doctorate in 1933. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1922–1951) and Aichi Gakuin University (1957–1977), publishing in law, Buddhist studies, and philosophy.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Seiji Kimura studied at Komazawa University (attested 1986). He subsequently held posts at Komazawa University (attested 1990) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995).
Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Seiji Kumagai completed his PhD at Kyoto University (~2004–2008) and became an associate professor there (~2013).
